plans.note: Article on Indemnification; Liability; Insurance is the natural home for any liability cap and consequential-damages waiver. Check whether the cap (if any) is mutual and whether carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement, willful misconduct) are symmetric; collaboration agreements often have an uncapped-but-mutual damages waiver only, which may still meet the fallback.

Expect reciprocal indemnities in sec-p0580. Assess whether RevMed indemnifies us for third-party IP claims arising from RevMed Background/Licensed Technology and for its own negligence/misconduct, and whether our indemnity is confined to our own Development/Commercialization acts. Cross-check IP warranties in sec-p0536 and sec-13.3.

Defined terms Competing Product, Non-SHP2 Same Class Product, Other SHP2 Inhibitor and SHP1/SHP2 criteria signal a mutual non-compete/field-restriction. Locate the covenant (likely in the LICENSE article as an exclusivity covenant or in RevMed/Sanofi covenants) and test the burden on us — scope by molecule class, term, and Acquiror Family/Change of Control carve-outs.

Exclusive licence grants in sec-p0246 may be paired with an obligation on us not to develop or in-license competing SHP2/SHP1 inhibitors; also check MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY for any obligation to source solely from RevMed. Note that exclusivity we receive is a benefit and should not be flagged.

No MFN concept appears in the defined terms or outline; the Royalty Floor and financial mechanics in sec-p0384 are the only plausible location. Confirm absence before marking missing, and remember an MFN running in our favour is welcome.

No employee non-solicit is evident; GENERAL PROVISIONS is the usual home, with a secondary possibility alongside FTE/personnel provisions in the RESEARCH article. If present, check duration and general-advertising carve-out.

TERM AND TERMINATION should contain termination at will (typically ours, by notice, product-by-product/country-by-country) plus termination for breach, insolvency and safety. Verify our notice period, that no termination fee or accelerated milestone is payable, and that RevMed lacks a convenience right.

Term here is likely tied to the royalty term/Regulatory Exclusivity rather than a renewing subscription term; check the Term provision in sec-p0484 for any automatic extension and notice window before concluding the rule is inapplicable.

Governing law, dispute resolution and venue will sit in GENERAL PROVISIONS. Confirm New York/Delaware/California/England & Wales and courts rather than foreign-seat arbitration; note escalation to Designated Senior Officers as a permitted pre-step.

Assignment clause in sec-p0605, read with the Change of Control, Acquiror Family and Acquired Party Family definitions in the DEFINITIONS article. Confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor in a merger/asset sale without consent, and that RevMed cannot terminate on our change of control.

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS governs ownership of Program Inventions, Joint Program Technology and Sanofi Sole Program Know-How/Patents. Verify we own inventions we make and the data we fund, that no Sanofi background IP is assigned to RevMed, and check prosecution/enforcement control for Sanofi Prosecuted Patents.

The LICENSE article should grant us rights under RevMed Licensed Technology in the Field and Licensed Territory. Confirm the grant extends to our Affiliates, Sublicensees and Permitted Contractors or Researchers, is not revocable at will, and that any sublicensing consent is not unreasonably withheld.

Royalty/Net Sales record-keeping and audit rights against us will be in FINANCIAL PROVISIONS. Test frequency (no more than annual), notice, use of an independent accountant, confidentiality, look-back period, and that RevMed bears the cost absent a material underpayment threshold.

No liquidated damages concept is signalled; check FINANCIAL PROVISIONS for interest on late payments and any diligence-failure payment, and sec-p0484 for termination fees, before concluding absence. Ordinary late-payment interest is not a penalty for this rule.

REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS plus RevMed's covenants in sec-13.3 are the operative warranties. Look for RevMed IP title/non-infringement, no-encumbrance, compliance with Applicable Law/FCPA and Excluded List reps, and for any broad disclaimer that would strip our remedy; also check GMP/supply warranties in sec-p0357.

The article heading expressly includes Insurance, so expect a mutual coverage covenant. Confirm RevMed carries commercially reasonable product liability/clinical trial cover at a stated limit for the Term plus a tail.

Milestones, royalties and Research/Development Budget cost-sharing are not take-or-pay commitments and should not be flagged. Check MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY for any minimum order or take-or-pay volume obligation on us and the diligence/Commercially Reasonable Efforts obligations in sec-p0303 and sec-p0362 for hard minimums.

Effects-of-termination provisions in sec-p0484 should cover wind-down of Clinical Trials, transfer of Regulatory Approvals and data, transition of Manufacturing and supply continuity, and sell-off rights. Confirm the assistance runs to us where RevMed terminates and that our data/Study Reports are returned.
